headline: NORMALIZATION was the next named-absent corpus item. Building it produced three findings bigger than the kernel: a WRITE-AFTER-READ hazard that WAS ALREADY IN SOFTMAX AND ATTENTION, a batching correction that flipped the MLX verdict from `no claim` to `we lose`, and a catastrophic-cancellation threshold measured rather than recited.

correctness.agreement_with_mlx_fast: 9.5e-07 on all four timed shapes, so our fused kernel computes what Apple's does

THE_HAZARD_AND_IT_WAS_ALREADY_ELSEWHERE.how_it_was_found: the top-k receipt one block earlier measured a missing barrier being EXACTLY CORRECT at threadgroup 64 and 256 and firing at 1024 in 16 of 30 runs, and concluded a control must be run ACROSS WIDTHS. Doing that here found something the control was not looking for: THE INTACT KERNEL WAS WRONG AT 1024.
THE_HAZARD_AND_IT_WAS_ALREADY_ELSEWHERE.cause: phase 1 writes red[warp], barriers, and then EVERY thread READS red[0..lanes). Phase 2 then WRITES red[warp] again with NOTHING ordering that write after those reads -- a write-after-read hazard, not a missing publish barrier. At 32 lanes the read loop is long enough for a fast thread to overtake a slow one.

AND_THE_SAME_SHAPE_WAS_ALREADY_IN_TWO_SH.reading: NEITHER FIRES, at any width, across 10 and 6 runs -- because a long exp loop sits between the read and the next write. But the previous receipt's own words apply: A RACE THAT DOES NOT FIRE IS NOT A PASSING TEST. Softmax and attention were not safe, they were UNCAUGHT, and their receipts measured them correct for many blocks.
AND_THE_SAME_SHAPE_WAS_ALREADY_IN_TWO_SH.fixed_structurally_not_by_evidence: the second reduction now gets ITS OWN SLOTS in all three lowerings. That beats adding a third barrier because there is nothing left to forget, and it costs 128 bytes of threadgroup memory at the widest setting.

the_barrier_control_itself_is_LOUD_here.why_it_differs_from_top_k: this barrier publishes the ROW MEAN, which every thread then reads -- a TOTAL dependency, so removing it is wrong 10 of 10 runs at every width (0.043 / 1.15 / 1.96). The top-k tree reduce's dependency is INCIDENTAL, which is why the same class of control was nearly silent there.

THE_BATCHING_CORRECTION_FLIPPED_THE_VERD.what_changed_and_why_it_matters: unbatched, 3 of 4 shapes returned NO_CLAIM and one INDISTINGUISHABLE -- a reader would have taken that as parity with Apple's hand-tuned primitive. Batched, with clean arms, MLX WINS at 0.87x, 0.91x and 0.70x. THE FIRST MEASUREMENT DID NOT SHOW PARITY, IT SHOWED AN INSTRUMENT THAT COULD NOT SEE, and reporting `no claim either way` would have let the flattering reading stand.

AND_THE_MACHINE_CONSTANT_PREDICTS_THE_DI.reading: six of the eight arms shed 0.10-0.20 ms per call, centred on the 0.157 ms the AirGraph sweep measured in unrelated work. The submission was COMMON MODE -- it did not bias the direction, it DILUTED the margin until the gate refused a real result, which is the third time this program has caught that exact instrument failure.

THE_BATCHING_CORRECTION_FLIPPED_THE_VERD.MLX_RETAINED: §141 and §142: the evidence says DO NOT REPLACE. Apple's fused primitive wins on every shape where the gate spoke.

the_cancellation_threshold_measured.prediction_before_the_run: relative variance error ~ (mean/sigma)^2; indistinguishable at ratio 1; f32's 24 bits exhausted near ratio 4096
the_cancellation_threshold_measured.verdict: CONFIRMED IN ALL THREE PARTS. At mean/sigma = 1 the two forms are indistinguishable (1.3e-07 vs 1.5e-07). The one-pass error grows roughly QUADRATICALLY -- 1.4e-05 at 16, 5.7e-03 at 256, 0.125 at 1024 -- and at 4096 it is NaN, which is where 24 bits of f32 were predicted to run out.
the_cancellation_threshold_measured.NaN_IS_WORSE_THAN_INACCURATE: E[x^2] - E[x]^2 goes NEGATIVE, so rsqrt(var + eps) is NaN. A negative variance is a physically impossible value that the arithmetic produces SILENTLY, and NaN then propagates through everything downstream.
the_cancellation_threshold_measured.two_pass_is_not_immune_and_that_is_state: its error also grows, 1.3e-07 to 1.8e-03 across the same sweep -- but LINEARLY in the ratio where one-pass is quadratic, and it never produces a NaN.
the_cancellation_threshold_measured.why_the_bug_survives_in_real_code: transformer hidden states have near-zero mean, so mean/sigma is O(1) and one-pass is SAFE EXACTLY WHERE PEOPLE TEST IT. It fails on a distribution shift, which is the worst place to discover it.
the_cancellation_threshold_measured.consequence_for_RMSNorm: RMSNorm subtracts no mean, so this hazard does not exist for it at all -- validate() REFUSES variance='one_pass' on rms rather than accepting a flag that means nothing.

claim_boundary.no_model: synthetic rows; this is the SHAPE of a transformer norm, not a model
claim_boundary.batched_arms_measure_a_different_thing: batching removes the per-call submission, so these numbers describe a norm inside a larger graph, not a norm submitted alone -- which is the realistic case and is stated rather than assumed
claim_boundary.one_NO_CLAIM_remains: layer 4096x4096 batched: MLX's own arm carried 40.4% IQR, so the gate refused despite a 24% margin. Not counted as a win for either side.
claim_boundary.softmax_and_attention_are_fixed_but_were: their correctness at every width is evidence of nothing about the hazard; the fix is structural
